brief: Goldman TMT sales note covering multiple threads. TSMC hit an all-time high after Musk confirmed preliminary talks on a TSMC role in Terafab's Texas chip project ($16.8bn initial, $55-119bn total planned spend); a partnership could cut execution risk but complicate Intel's role, no deal yet, next catalyst TSMC's 15 October call. GS semis analyst Jim is constructive into Q3 after the SOX's 11% pullback, preferring AMAT, STX and MCHP into earnings and seeing QCOM, KLAC and WDC as relatively less attractive, with SemiCap and memory (MCHP, NXP, ADI) favored on improving visibility. Schneider Electric's $23.7bn all-cash deal for PTC ($205/share, 42% premium) raises competitive pressure on Dassault Systemes but does not threaten it near-term; family control (~40%) complicates any DSY takeover. BT confirmed buying TalkTalk/PlatformX, c£400m FY27 cash impact, guidance unchanged. GS upgrades Stagwell to Buy ($13 PT) and initiates Havas at Neutral (€19 PT) as agency growth reaccelerates to ~6%. Separately, Goldman flags Q3 S&P 500 earnings increasingly AI-driven (27% EPS growth, hyperscaler capex +116%) and hyperscaler debt issuance scaling toward $420bn by 2027, pressuring long-end yields.
